A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Lumos-1, with matching core methods, experiments and qualitative examples. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original GenEval and VBench evaluations, masking and RoPE ablations, inference timings and generated examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original evaluations and adds fine-tuned model results, controlled training-strategy and RoPE comparisons, and efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The architecture, MM-RoPE and AR-DF algorithms remain intact, but Section 3.3 adds a final supervised fine-tuning stage using approximately 100k images and 20k videos. Section 3.2 also changes the stated loss targets from unmasked to masked tokens; this corrects the description without establishing that the earlier implementation differed.

E1.justification: Both versions cover text-to-image, image-to-video and text-to-video generation using GenEval and VBench, including the same aspect-ratio scenarios. The added small-scale image/video fine-tuning data have no stated distinct domain or population. The proposed understanding tasks in Appendix F.1 are future work, not evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The GenEval comparison adds numerous methods, including Meissonic, Muddit, SANA 1.5, Fluid, Show-o2 and Lumina-mGPT variants, while removing SD v2.1 and LWM from that table. VBench-I2V adds VideoMAR and VBench-T2V adds NOVA. New controlled comparisons evaluate alternative loss-weighting strategies and U-RoPE, IL-RoPE, VideoRoPE and HoPE.

E3.justification: v2 adds fine-tuning experiments and 512×512 GenEval evaluations, plus controlled 1B-model studies trained for 10k steps on eight H20 GPUs. The reported T2V resolution changes from 448×256×25 to 672×384×25. Table D1 also changes the 3B model's 384p learning rate from 2.5e-5 to 5.0e-5; these reported revisions do not establish which earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained validation-loss curves, v2 adds downstream generation comparisons of tube masking against random masking, loss reweighting and diffusion forcing, and quantitative MM-RoPE component and scaling ablations. It also tests alternative RoPE designs, decoding strategies and training efficiency in Tables 5–8 and E4. The earlier aspect-ratio and meta-group analyses are retained in Appendix E.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the experiments. The added tables retain point-estimate reporting, and the existing plotted analyses are unchanged.

E6.justification: The original GenEval scores of 0.601/0.664 remain, while v2 adds fine-tuned 512×512 results of 0.725/0.791. T2V adds fine-tuned totals of 78.17/78.90 and revises the non-fine-tuned 1.5B result under a changed resolution. Show-o's reported GenEval score changes from 0.53 to 0.68. New results also cover masking, RoPE alternatives, decoding speed and training costs; the changed settings preclude treating all differences as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The RoPE identities, MM-RoPE construction and AR-DF masking equations are retained. Appendix B in v2 reproduces the detailed RoPE preliminaries previously presented in the main text; it introduces no new proof, theorem or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain LLM-compatible video generation through MM-RoPE and AR-DF. The abstract strengthens the performance claim from comparability with EMU3, COSMOS-Video2World and OpenSoraPlan to surpassing Show-o2, COSMOS-Video2World and OpenSoraPlan, supported partly by newly reported fine-tuned results.

C2.justification: Appendix A adds an interpretation of AR-DF as mitigating drift and error accumulation, distinguishing this from FramePack's emphasis on forgetting. Appendix E.2 explains differences among RoPE alternatives and acknowledges possible gains from tuning VideoRoPE. Appendix F.1 adds a detailed roadmap and prerequisites for understanding-generation unification, while retaining the original limitations concerning data scale and complex motion.

D1.justification: v2 adds fine-tuning sample counts, controlled-experiment budgets, VideoRoPE's default-parameter disclosure and normalized training-cost information. Most architecture, tokenizer, sequence-formatting and memory-saving details are retained or relocated. A new reproducibility statement promises code, weights and evaluation scripts upon publication alongside the existing repository link; actual availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix A substantially expand positioning against alternative RoPEs, LLM-based generators, Diffusion Forcing and FramePack. New citations include HoPE, UniViT, Mogao, Show-o2 and several discrete-diffusion generators. Architectural and RoPE design comparisons make the claimed distinctions more explicit; the earlier image-generation related work is relocated rather than removed.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and introduction around two challenges and adds an explicit contribution list. It reorganizes related work, mathematical preliminaries, implementation details and analyses between the main text and expanded appendices, moves references before the appendix, and adds ethics, reproducibility and LLM-use statements. The title also explicitly identifies discrete diffusion.

P2.justification: The two-column body becomes predominantly single-column with inset tables. Benchmark tables gain representation-type columns and fine-tuning annotations, and new design, ablation, comparison and cost tables are introduced. Existing figures and qualitative examples are retained but repositioned; v1 Figure 9 becomes Figure E1, and some new comparison tables are repeated in the appendix.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the central designs: Tables 5 and 7–8 extend v1's loss-curve evidence to downstream generation metrics and relevant alternatives, while Table 6 directly tests decoding efficiency. Broader comparisons and clearer positioning address important evidential gaps. Higher headline scores involve fine-tuning and changed resolutions, and uncertainty reporting remains absent, but the added controlled evidence materially improves the paper's overall support.
